method: Pressure = z-score of a node's 4-week change (and its level, for spreads, rates and ratios) against its own last 3 years; + is tightening or stress, - is easing. A link is 'passing' when both ends are at least 0.75 and moving the way the link says; a 'gap' is when the upstream end is at least 1.25 and the downstream end has not followed. Link strength = correlation of non-overlapping 4-week changes since 2010 (or since the data starts), signed so positive means it behaves as the theory says.

nodes.label: Fed balance sheet
nodes.what: Total Fed assets. Shrinking (QT) drains cash from the system.

nodes.label: Fed policy rate
nodes.what: Effective fed funds rate. Higher means money costs more.

nodes.label: Reverse repo cushion
nodes.what: Cash parked at the Fed overnight. A thin cushion means less spare cash to absorb shocks.

nodes.label: Treasury auctions
nodes.what: How well new Treasury supply is absorbed: bid-to-cover and the share dealers are left holding.

nodes.label: Oil
nodes.what: WTI crude. Rising oil feeds inflation worries and, for Canada, the currency.

nodes.label: Repo funding
nodes.what: SOFR minus fed funds. When overnight secured money costs more than policy, cash is scarce.
nodes.src: FRED SOFR, DFF; NY Fed via credit tracker

nodes.label: 10y Treasury yield
nodes.what: The price of long-term money for everyone.

nodes.label: Real yields
nodes.what: 10-year TIPS yield: what money earns after inflation. Weighs on long-duration growth stocks.

nodes.label: US dollar
nodes.what: Broad trade-weighted dollar. A rising dollar tightens money for the rest of the world.

nodes.label: Financial conditions
nodes.what: Chicago Fed NFCI: 100+ measures of how easy it is to borrow and raise money.

nodes.label: Corporate credit
nodes.what: High-yield bond spread over Treasuries. Widening means lenders want more to take risk.
nodes.src: FRED ICE BofA HY OAS (3 years kept)

nodes.label: VIX curve
nodes.what: VIX divided by 3-month VIX. Above 1 (backwardation) means near-term fear exceeds longer-term.

nodes.label: Futures positioning
nodes.what: CFTC: how hedge funds and asset managers are positioned in S&P and VIX futures. Crowding is fragility, not direction.
nodes.src: CFTC Traders in Financial Futures via analyses/flows/flows.py

nodes.label: Margin debt
nodes.what: FINRA customer margin balances. High leverage amplifies falls through margin calls.

nodes.label: S&P 500
nodes.what: US large caps. Falling counts as pressure.

nodes.label: Nasdaq
nodes.what: Growth and tech heavy. Most sensitive to real yields.

nodes.label: ETF flows
nodes.what: SPY creations and redemptions, and the forced end-of-day rebalancing of leveraged ETFs.

nodes.label: Canada (USD/CAD)
nodes.what: CAD per USD. Rising means a weaker loonie, which usually comes with risk-off or falling oil.
nodes.src: FRED DEXCAUS; Bank of Canada via canada tracker
